messages.text: Clara found the little Raleigh courthouse card you tucked in her book. She wants to know if Granddaddy has more in the upstairs room.
Tell her I have a shoebox of them on the north table. I was putting them in sleeves while the trumpet record was on.
She also asked if you still have the tiny brush set for making houses.
Yes. I need to clear space beside the easel first, but she can pick a mill town scene Sunday.
Dad, did you see the county board forum clip? They finally asked about bus routes and classroom aides.
I watched the middle part after supper. I wrote down who had an actual answer and who just talked around it.
My fifth graders asked about the courthouse mural again. I told them we can talk about hard parts of town history without turning it into a chant.
That sounds about right. The hard parts ought to be talked about, but some signs and shouting lose me.
The one with the D beside her name had the clearest school answer, honestly.
The school board forum is Thursday. Are you still going, or did the pothole meeting win?
Going to both if my knee behaves. I want to hear numbers, not speeches.
Fair. Also the PTA forum has a question box about vest cameras and how calls with someone spiraling get handled.
For that seat I am looking at the plan first. If the buses and classroom numbers make sense, the little letter is not the main thing.
I'd rather hear specifics like that than slogans. Training and a clear record of what happened would do more than folks talking past each other.
Please ask about the teacher aide slots if they take questions.
I wrote that down beside road resurfacing and the community college trades grant.
Clara wants to know if Granddaddy can see her drawing after your laptop night.
Tell her yes. I have to finish the ACC-201 quiz before 9, then I can look.
She will hold you to that. Do you still have the Thursday evening session too?
Yes, just Tuesdays and Thursdays this term. Keeps it manageable with the lead training at work.
Mama says Mrs. Teague sent her one of those loud screenshots again. Something about what to avoid this spring.
Tell Mama not to act off that. I will ask the pharmacist when I pick up her refill and check the clinic page after work.
Got it. She also wants to know if the warm soak is okay for her hands tonight.
Warm soak is fine if it helps, but if the swelling is still there tomorrow I want her calling the office.
Mama asked if you were still coming through Angier Saturday. She mentioned lunch at Holt Lake again.
I will come by, but I am bringing ham sandwiches in the cooler. Need to let the March drafts finish first.
Got it. I will tell her not to fuss over it. I can pick up bananas and crackers Friday.
Thanks. I may still stop at the BP for coffee if I leave before daylight.
Mama said Mrs. Albright called again about that little table by her back door.
I told her I would tighten the leg after my route Friday, so I will. I can carry Mama's refill list over the same trip.
Good. I will call Mama after lunch tomorrow and tell her not to fool with it herself.
I'll put the small wrench set in the truck tonight so I don't forget.
Boss asked if I could stay late again. How did you ever keep saying no without getting on somebody's list?
I learned to ask what it paid, what it cost at home, and whether the light bill was already covered.
So not just grabbing every extra hour.
Not if Diane had plates ready and you and Emily were waiting at the table.
You still got that old navy jacket with the zipper pockets? Mine finally gave up after crawling around two units today.
It is hanging by the back door. Grease on one sleeve but the pockets still hold keys, scanner, and receipts.
That is all I need. Raleigh traffic ate me alive today. I don't know how folks sit in those glass buildings all day.
I had my chance at one of those after Wake Tech. I still like being able to stop, stretch my knees, and keep moving.
Saw one of those battery vans at a service call today. Thing was quiet enough I didn't hear it pull in.
I'd like to try one on the downtown loop sometime. Fewer stops for fuel and less backtracking if the stops are grouped right.
You already got a spreadsheet for that, don't you.
A rough one. Also added a column for the two newer guys who keep missing the same apartment entrances.
Clara found the little blue-roof card you mailed last month and wants to know if you can make one with a porch swing.
Tell her I can try. Diane still has that old porch-swing photo from our first Benson rental if I can find the box.
She said the swing needs a cat on it too. Mark may come Sunday, so maybe bring the paints then.
I will set aside the small brush and a couple blank cards before supper.
Clara asked if Granddaddy saw the picture I posted from her book character day.
I saw it after supper. Diane had to show me where you tucked it in the album.
Dad, the book I mentioned has a chapter on courthouse records and who got written down as 'trouble' in old town files. You might notice museum overlap.
She also wants you to see the spring carnival notice. It is on the school page with the bake sale times.
That is exactly where my mind went. Darnell and I were talking at lunch about how a file can sound official and still miss half the story.
I will check that one tomorrow morning. I like having the dates where I can find them again.
I would like to hear more Sunday if Mark does not turn it into a joke.
We can keep it at the table and civil. I am not looking for a big scene, just want to understand it better.
Mama said the morning box was empty but I think she meant Wednesday only. Can you look at your copy before I call the pharmacy?
I have the refill sheet in the truck folder. I marked Wed AM twice because that row looked easy to miss.
Got it. Try not to redo the whole chart before work.
Too late on the colored lines. But I stopped before alphabetizing the pill bottles.
Mama said the fellowship hall is doing beans and slaw Friday. She wants to know if you still have Daddy's folding table.
I do. One leg sticks, but I can free it up before I bring it.
Good. Also Mark asked if you saw that clip from the Charlotte practice today.
Not yet. I had the Bulls score alert open while fixing the pantry latch, so I'll catch it after supper.
Mama found that metal recipe box again. It had Daddy's pay envelopes, a yellow route card, and one of her old adding-machine ribbons tucked behind the pound cake card.
Mama found that old Angier school picture while looking for the insurance card.
Sounds like her. Anything from the Angier house worth keeping for Emily?
Put it aside if you can. Diane wants to scan a few before the supper next week.
Yes. A photo of us on the porch, you about sixteen, me looking mad because Mama made me stand still. Daddy's work shirt is hanging over the rail in it.
Got it. She also found the little hospital bracelet envelope with 3/12 written on it.
That sounds like Mama. She kept every scrap from Angier.
Keep that one. Diane will want to see the porch and Mama's neat little numbers on the back.
You still near Garner? I can swing by after my last service call if you're back.
Just turned in the clinic totes and two parts boxes. Should be home close to 5 after I fuel the van.
Long Friday. Your check hit today or next one?
Today. Same every other Friday. Diane already has the BlueCross draft and house payment marked.
I found your yellow pad under the coupons. It has Charleston mileage on one side and Asheville cabin names on the other.
Leave it there if you don't mind. I still need to match the fuel estimate to the Friday route.
Also the little jar has $112 in it after I put in the grocery change. I did not touch the bill envelopes.
Good. I will add it to the sheet tonight and see if spring still looks possible.
I left the copay slips beside your laptop. Can you put the orthodontist refund and the $538.20 draft on the March tab?
Yes. I have the blue notebook open and will mark them before I take the short loop through town.
Good. Also Dr. Vance asked me to come in Monday 8:30-1:00 instead of Tuesday, so don't set Mama's refill run for that morning.
Moving it to Monday afternoon. That keeps the pharmacy, bank, and grocery stop in one pass.
I put the pill splitter back in the top drawer. Did you already do tomorrow morning's little half?
Yes, set beside the coffee mug so I don't miss it before church.
Good. I also packed the blue cold pack in case the steps at Mama's make you favor that leg again.
Thanks. I'm trying to keep the plate light tonight too. Still aiming for that 15 before summer.
Mama said the porch light is out again. If you come by Angier, can you bring that socket tester?
I can. I already have the tester and jumper cables in the truck. Need to stop for washer fluid first.
Got it. Diane mentioned you were sorting bills too. Do you still want me to wait on sending you that dentist receipt?
Send it. I paid the house this morning and the card is small enough to cover Friday with the groceries.
Shop guys were asking if your route has anybody who bargains for you on raises.
Nope. Just me and the route manager. I keep my own notes before the yearly sit-down.
Gotcha. You still doing that museum desk thing tomorrow after deliveries?
Yes, 10 to 1. Then home to stretch canvas if my knees are not barking.
You coming by tomorrow? I can grab wings. I know you will nurse one bottle all game anyway.
Tomorrow works. Tea is fine for me after the first one. Knee is acting up so I am keeping the stronger stuff in the cabinet unless I really have to.
Fair. Also do not open that school board clip I sent after 9. The replies under it are a mess.
Then send me the short version when I get there. I would rather hear it from you than read twenty strangers swinging at each other.
I put the green beans in the carrier. Mrs. Calhoun still needs a ride for the 10:45 start.
I can pick her up after I stack chairs in the hall. Tell Tom I will skip the front row today if the family with the new baby needs it.
That sounds right. Also, the youth table asked if you could help carry the canned goods boxes before we eat.
Yes. I would rather be useful in the kitchen than argue over who sat where.
I set your small brush cup by the sink. Supper can wait if you want to take Pine Street first.
Thanks. I need to make a short list for Monday, then I'll walk before the chicken goes in.
That sounds fine. The blue record sleeve is still on the table if you were looking for it.
Good. I'll sit with that and the little mill picture after we eat.
If your knees are decent after church, I can meet you by the club lot before supper.
That works. I need to loosen up after that Raleigh run and all those stoplights.
Bring the blue band from the hall closet. You said it helped your back last time.
I'll put it by my keys so I don't forget it.
Clara asked if Granddaddy still has the picture of the little white store near Angier.
I do. It was beside the road before they widened it. I'll bring it Sunday if I can find the box.
Clara asked if the little room with the blue quilt is still hers for Saturday.
It is when she comes. Diane already put the crayons back in the nightstand.
She will love that. Fuquay traffic took us 28 minutes just to get across town today.
Thank you. I know it has been since January, but she remembers every corner of that room.
That's how it starts. First cones, then more lanes, then the old places get hard to recognize.
We will move my route papers off the bed and keep supper simple for the three of you when you drop her.
Clara asked if Granddaddy still has the little red store picture from Main Street.
It is on the drying board. I only got the roofline right after supper last night.
She wants to bring her own brush next Sunday if that is not too much.
That is fine. I may take her by the old feed store first if the light is decent.
The Raleigh clinic moved her 10:20 slot to 11:05 Friday. I can take that one before work.
Good. I will come through Angier Saturday morning for Food Lion and the loose rail by the back steps.
Check the pill box too. She had Tuesday sitting where Thursday ought to be.
I will bring a fresh chart with bigger print. I need to be back before Clara gets dropped off at 4.
If you pass Food Lion, grab cornmeal and a small bag of flour. I can do the pan bread with the beans tonight.
Did dispatch keep you on the Raleigh run until five again?
Close. Two late signatures, then I need to be home by 6:30 for the live class room.
Will do. I also pulled two early peppers from the back row, not enough for much but they can go in the pot.
I left the worksheet open. It still shows 5,600 on the top line and 4,300 after deductions.
That works. And no stopping for a big plate on the way home after what the nurse circled last week.
I hear you. Just groceries and home.
Good. I will check groceries and the insurance draft after the lecture.
My fourth graders asked why the old depot photo only shows the owners. Do you ever run into that with those old boxes you sort?
Clara found a folded road sheet in your jacket pocket and asked if it was a treasure map.
More than I used to notice. A whole stack will have names on storefronts, then three unlabeled families standing right beside them.
Tell her it got me around that Fuquay school traffic better than the blue line did this morning.
I put it on the counter with the little notebook. There are numbers all down the side, so I did not let her color on it.
That sounds like exactly the kind of thing kids should learn to ask about.
Good save. I still need those times when I fill out the run sheet tonight.
I wrote a note for the case card so Ruth can check it Saturday. No speech, just adding who is missing when we know it.
Clara taped your little courthouse painting beside her bed. She wants to know if the blue windows were from a real building.
Tell her they were from the old photo in that Johnston County booklet. I changed the roof because the picture was too dark.
She also found your paper with all the tiny numbered boxes and asked why Granddaddy writes in squares.
That was last night's page before bed. I got stuck on 37 down and left it on the kitchen table.
Mama said you marked up that voter mailer again. You and your little notes.
Somebody has to check who voted for the tax package and who just talks tough on TV.
I already know my column.
I mostly do too, but I still want the one who can keep the roads passable and not waste payroll.
I can take Mama to the 9:40 appointment Friday. Are you still tied up after supper tonight?
I am. Pearson lockbox opens at 6 and I have a chapter check due before bed.
Got it. I will call Mama after lunch and tell her Saturday is better for your grocery run.
Thanks. This one is on budgets and scheduling, so it ought to help with the crew-lead interview too.
I put your library bag by the door. It has the Plato paperback, the Mars one, and the courthouse notes.
Thank you. I need the pencil too. Last week Jim caught me on one word because I wrote in pen.
Pencil is clipped to the front. Supper will be covered, so don't rush back.
I'll be home a little after 8 if they don't get sidetracked on the mill fire.
You have walked past the pantry three times and moved the cereal twice. Come sit with me a minute.
I was making sure tomorrow's Angier list matched Linda's text. Then I noticed the shelves were backward.
The shelves can survive. I still have those two numbers from Debbie at church if you ever want a plain hour with somebody who just listens.
Keep them. I am not saying no. I just don't know what I would say first.
Clara asked if Granddaddy is eating with us Sunday or doing another long route.
Tell her I marked myself off after 4. I already checked the mortgage and insurance drafts.
She will save you the green crayon then.
Good. I can miss an extra run before I miss that.
Clara wants to know if Granddaddy can still walk to the park after supper Sunday.
Tell her yes if we keep it flat. I overdid the ladder work yesterday and took one from the brown bottle at lunch.
Flat route works. Mom said you were writing numbers from that arm cuff again, so I won't bring the salty casserole.
Appreciate it. I'll bring strawberries instead of pie.
Clara asked why Granddaddy draws streets on graph paper instead of houses now.
Tell her the houses are still coming. These streets are for a small idea with three Garner shops that don't want boxes sitting on porches all afternoon.
That sounds like the kind of thing you'd keep fair and on time.
That's the hope. If I can show the young ones a cleaner way to load the van, maybe it saves them a few headaches too.
Clara wants to know if Granddaddy can show her the little tobacco barn model again when we come Sunday.
I can bring the photo cards from the heritage desk. They let me keep the extra set after the fourth graders came through.
She will love that. Also, thank you for what you said last week about the parents who came in late. I know some folks were muttering.
I have been late enough in my own life to keep quiet. People usually need a hand more than a lecture.
One of the teacher group chats is passing around a post in giant letters. I am not forwarding it to you because I know your face already.
Good. If it has no link or name on it, it can stay in that group chat.
Fair. Clara says your knee needs the blue heating pad before you come paint with her.
She may be right. I will use it tonight, and I already left a message for Dr. Harris about what I can do before Sunday.
Mama's refill is handled. Also, that school board mailer came to her house again.
Leave it on her table and I will look Saturday. I want to compare it with the road-widening answer from the forum.
Mama said your back was hurting after moving that box. Did you take what the dentist gave you last year?
No. I used the heating pad and two regular tablets from the kitchen bottle. I do not like fooling with the old white ones unless a doctor says so.
You and those forums. I already know which side I trust.
On Raleigh stuff maybe. For county seats I want the person who has read the school budget and knows where the ambulances are thin.
Got it. Also I am done with that thread from Eddie. People are showing themselves.
Leave it alone and call me after work if you want. Ten minutes on the phone beats typing at folks all afternoon.
Ray still need that hand truck Saturday? I can bring mine if yours is buried.
Mine is by the mower. Ray has two file cabinets to get out of his shop before noon.
You and your Saturday projects.
He helped me swap that battery last winter. I said I would come, so I will be there at 8:30.
I put the leftover cake in the Benson fridge before work.
Thanks. I am carrying the Angier photos to Mama tomorrow and will stop by the pharmacy too.
Take the envelope from 1969 if Linda packed it. Your mother said it was in the same box.
I saw it by the scanner. I will bring it back after she looks through it.
The bank posted 3,250 from the courier company this morning. I moved grocery and insurance money like we planned.
Good. The route sheet showed 4,300 before the usual deductions, so that matches close enough.
I left the museum mileage off the income page and put your paint paper under supplies.
That is right. Those two belong nowhere near the courier line.
Do you still want me to meet you at Smithfield's after work or should I start the chicken thighs?
Start the chicken. Brake repair hit harder than I liked, and the water draft comes out Monday.
That is fine. I have rice and green beans, and you can take the leftovers tomorrow.
Perfect. I already bought coffee at Handy Mart this morning, so home food tonight is smarter.
When you leave the plant, can you stop for the refill and the low-salt crackers before tomorrow's Angier run?
Yes. I also need to price the hinge for that cabinet door.
I put the mortgage draft and my brake repair in the budget sheet, so just keep the receipt.
Got it. I have class reading after supper, then I will pack the chart and tools.
Clara asked if the little painted houses are from the place with the lavender card on your fridge.
Tell her not yet. That card is staying there until the jar catches up.
She wants to help you color the map lines again Sunday, if you bring the notebook.
Clara wants to know if Granddaddy can bring the little blue screwdriver Sunday. Her toy stove door is loose again.
I can bring it. I already have the Charleston pages clipped separate so she can pick a postcard spot.
I'll bring it. Tell her we don't toss a good stove over one screw.
She also asked if the bull on your phone won last night. I think she means the app notification she saw.
Tell her not last night, but there's another one after supper. I'll show her the little field picture if she's still awake.
Clara asked if Granddaddy still has the tiny paint cakes. She wants another little house next Sunday.
I do. I was using them tonight after I wrote out tomorrow's errands.
She also said your trumpet music makes the kitchen feel like a movie.
Tell her I kept the brushes clean this time. I took a short walk first, so the picture came out steadier.
Mama wants to know if you saw Cousin Ray's birthday pictures. She said everybody is commenting under them.
Not yet. I usually look at those after work when I am at the desktop.
Also the Angier street fair posted the vendor list. Barbecue truck is back.
Send me the notice if you can. I want to keep that Saturday open if Diane is free.
Brake place treat y'all decent? I can look at the old pads Sunday if they gave them back.
They kept them, but the receipt says rotors, pads, and one caliper line. $612.48 total.
Ouch. That'll make your little home ledger mad.
Already did. March is sitting at $4,603 with two grocery receipts still in my shirt pocket.
My truck is doing that squeal on startup again. Shop wants $410 just to do belt and tensioner.
Bring it Sunday if you can. We can price the parts first and see if it is simple enough in the driveway.
That would help. I hate dropping that much right now.
If it has to be done, $400 will not sink us this month. I would rather check the belt before anybody charges labor.
I can swing by Sunday after the Raleigh job. Need laundry and whatever Mom is cooking.
Diane is making roast if the oven behaves. Emily said Clara wants the little houses at the table again.
I'll bring my work shirts. Also found that old baseball glove in my closet if you want it out of there.
Bring it. The guest room still has your bin beside Emily's school boxes.
Late call in Garner. If I get done after midnight, can I use the couch and throw my work shirts in before breakfast?
Couch is open. Your old basket is still in the hall closet, same as last time.
I think last time was around Thanksgiving. I will be quiet if I roll in.
Diane and I will leave the porch light on and two towels by the washer.
I laid the scanned papers in the dining room. Your mama's pencil columns are easier to read than our bank app.
She would still catch a missing dime. Did you see Daddy's ticket with Angier Lumber stamped crooked?
I did. Also that grocery receipt from 1979 made me wince. Four people and every line counted.
That was about right. Mama stretched it and Daddy kept that truck moving.
Mama asked if you were coming to Angier this morning or doing that downtown thing first.
Downtown first. I only have the card file until noon, then I can pick up her bread and stop by.
Mama said wear the shirt with the snaps if you are fixing that shelf after her groceries. She remembers you tearing the other one.
Already wearing it. Same boots too. I can hit her pharmacy after my last Apex stop.
Got it. She found two old Main Street postcards in Daddy's desk if you want to look before she gives them away.
Tell her to hold them. Sometimes the back tells more than the picture, especially if there is a name nobody copied onto the front label.
Got it. I found that old Raleigh application in her file box with your school papers, by the way.
Leave it there for now. Funny what we keep.
When you come through Angier, Mama needs milk and the blue lid ointment.
Got it. I am leaving Benson by the creek road so I can stop five minutes at that leaning barn.
As long as you are not late for her pills.
I won't be. I just want the morning edge on the field before the clouds thicken.
Mama found three old fairground cards in Daddy's desk. Do you want them or should I leave them here?
Mama found Paul's old receipt from Johnston County in her recipe drawer. I put it with the rest of his mess from that night he blew over after Smithfield.
Bring them when you come by. I have a county fair section started and need the postmark years.
Good. I don't need that mixed in with Mama's papers. My glove box has enough old blue-light notes from work routes without Paul's stack getting added.
You still going to that meeting after supper? I saw the flyer talking about cameras and extra help on calls where folks are out of control.
Got it. Diane said your back table is already full.
Yes. I want to hear the details, not a shouting match. A camera and better backup would settle half the stories before they grow legs.
It is, but I can move the wet canvas before supper. I had Sketches of Spain on and lost track of the stacks.
You running parcels today or can I swing by before lunch?
Half route this morning, then I have to upload that BUS 302 case before midnight.
Got it. Mom said the brake bill is why the March sheet is tight.
Yes. Last sheet only gave us 4,300 to place after everything came out.
Linda called. She said Mama is fine but she does not want Sunday supper turning into another courthouse records debate.
I hear her. Emily asked because of her class unit, and Darnell's story was still on my mind.
Just keep your voice even. Mark will poke at it if he thinks everyone is getting too serious.
I will. I would rather talk it through with family than spend Saturday in that crowd by the courthouse.
Are y'all still doing supper at 5? Clara wants to bring the little basket she decorated.
Five is good. Tell her she can pick the yellow squash if the ground dries out a little.
She'll love that. I can bring the slaw, but please don't send us home with six bags like last time.
No promises. I already owe Mr. Pate a couple of tomatoes for those eggs he dropped off.
You still got that old atlas in the truck? Mine would be dust by now.
It earns its spot. The tablet kept spinning near Garner, so I checked the page by the steering wheel.
Fair. Screen goes dumb right when you need it.
I wrote the mileage in the book and matched it to the file once I got home.
Mama said the survey ribbons are back on the Johnson place. Same corner by the church cemetery.
I saw them Saturday. That lane used to be nothing but pines and the old well cap.
Now everyone cuts through there when 210 backs up. I'll call Mama after lunch about her refills.
Thanks. I'll swing by next weekend and take the back road while it's still open.
Could you pick up Clara Thursday if my grade meeting runs over?
Thursday is tight. I have the courthouse pouch first thing, then WakeMed envelopes, then a small-shop run in Cary.
No worries. Mom said your vacation hours reset this month, so I wasn't sure if you had a short day.
Not that day. I am trying to keep the week around 42 and be back by 4 if dispatch doesn't add anything.
They called again about the 6 to 8 slot. I can stretch the chicken if you take it, but I know what you wrote on the fridge.
Leave it be. The copay cleared and Duke Energy is set for the 24th.
Then I will keep your plate warm for 5:45.
That sounds better than two more hours on the clock.
Mama said you were stopping by Saturday. Can you bring the pill chart printout too?
Yes. I may be a little later. I told Reggie I'd ride along with Caleb first and see why his morning run keeps running 20 minutes over.
Got it. Don't let them keep you all day.
I won't. If I can fix the order of stops and explain it plain, it keeps him from catching grief twice.
Mama asked if you're still going to Benson after supper tonight or coming to Angier.
Benson library tonight. Angier Saturday morning. I marked the pill chart for then.
Got it. She also said you left a stack of old Main Street photos here.
Keep them on the table if you can. I want to compare them with the chapter about the town moving toward the railroad.
You still keeping those old sneakers in the truck? Saw them when I grabbed the socket set.
Yes. Easier to stop near Benson when the route ends early instead of going straight home stiff.
Fair. My knees complain just riding to Wilson and back.
That's why I keep the band and shoes where I can see them.
Saw you at the chamber breakfast photo. Since when do you do eggs with council folks?
You around Saturday? I might bring laundry and look at that socket set.
Free coffee and the shop owners were asking good questions about license delays.
Saturday after noon works. I am on the laptop tonight until I upload the Excel case.
Did anybody say how that HVAC training money is supposed to work?
Excel case sounds like a fun night.
Yes. Matching funds, no new building until enrollment proves out. That is the kind of answer I like.
Better than freezing under a truck. It counts toward the plan Mr. Hales wants before he moves me up.
The bank app shows the Accord draft on the 24th. Is that the last big one or one more after?
I put your khakis in the dryer but left the brown work pants on the washer. They still had red clay at the cuffs.
One more small one after March, then that line is finished. I wrote it beside the house payment.
Brown ones for tomorrow, then. Museum dock in the morning and the Clayton loop after lunch.
Mrs. Albright from church asked if you ever regretted not taking that Raleigh office opening when you finished at Wake Tech.
Good. I will leave the Visa where you can see it and keep the grocery run normal.
No need to drag that out over supper. I would rather have tomorrow's pants ready.
Walgreens called back. The pharmacist said he can talk after 4 if you bring the card from Dr. Harris.
That works. The tire money stays untouched unless something actually breaks.
I will stop there after my route. I also bookmarked the CDC page the nurse mentioned, so I can compare it with what he says.
Good. Please do the Epsom soak before bed too. You were limping in the kitchen.
I will soak it, but I am still keeping the Monday appointment unless they tell me different.
Mom said you made a new binder tab for Grandma's afternoon pills. Clara would approve of the colors.
Tell Clara the purple tab means check the date before touching anything. I may have overdone it.
Clara asked if Granddaddy grew up where Great-Grandma still lives.
Tell her yes, same Angier roads, just fewer stoplights back then.
Overdone is still better than guessing. Also, if you use one of those numbers Mom saved, I can keep Clara an extra hour that day.
She wants to draw your old house beside the Benson house.
I appreciate that. I put the card behind my license so I do not lose it.
Have her leave room for Diane's flowers out front. That is the part she will notice.
You keeping that sample sheet in the truck console again? Saw it when I grabbed my hoodie.
Yes. I still need to mark the town board names after I read the zoning answers.
That new subdivision by 210 is going to make traffic ugly either way.
That is why I am checking who has a real growth map, not just the same old yard signs.
I found the cedar box under the towels. The courthouse picture is in there with the Raleigh hotel receipt.
Good. I need it for the April card before I forget.
Emily also left Clara's paper on the counter. She drew three houses and wrote your name on the biggest one.
I will put it by the paint tray. Mark's work shirts are still in the dryer too.
The azaleas by Mrs. Cole's fence look pretty right now. You may want your camera before the light drops.
I brought it. If I get one good frame I will put it with the other porch and flower shots tonight.
Mark asked if you saw his laundry joke from last night. It is under Emily's supper picture.
I missed that. I will look when we get home before I sort the azalea edits.
Clara wants to bring one old family picture for her class timeline. Is the Angier porch one okay, or is it too fragile?
Use the copy. Original stays in the sleeve. I was sixteen in that one and Linda kept making faces between takes.
She noticed the patch on Granddaddy's shirt and the stack of blank invoice pads beside Grandma. Children catch everything.
Tell her those pads paid for a lot of beans and gas when there was not much extra.

Club first if the rain holds off. Then I'll head to her place and fix that cabinet latch.
